title: Legacy /templates paths disagree with the TSD /admin/templates paths
source: Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 12; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2
description: The legacy story declares the five template operations as GET /templates, POST /templates, GET /templates/{templateId}/content, POST /templates/{templateId}/approve and POST /templates/{templateId}/withdraw on the legacy base path. TSD P6 T-A.1 names the same five as API-P6-003 to API-P6-007 under /admin/templates, /admin/templates/{templateId}/content, /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve and /admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw. The two names cannot both be the contract and the sources do not reconcile them.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 12 table row 1 'GET /templates'; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 row API-P6-003 'GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/templates'
proposed: Build the five operations under /admin/templates on /api/recovery/comms/v1 as TSD P6 T-A.1 names them; keep the legacy /templates names only as a record in section 12.1 and in the Data column of TC-E1-034-11.

title: Legacy 'set current' has no operation in the target contract
source: Legacy RWB-E1-034 AC2 and section 4 step 7; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1
description: Legacy AC2 acts on a version by choosing 'set current', and legacy flow step 7 has TemplateCatalog return the version as current from its valid from. The target contract has five template operations and none of them sets a version current; no source states the rule that makes a version current in the service, and no source names a set-current operation or its refusal.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-034 AC2 'When "LIT-0101" chooses set current on version 3'; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P6-003 to API-P6-007 with no set-current operation
proposed: Build no set-current operation: the current version of a code and language on a date is the Approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date, derived on read; AC2 is kept word for word and its refusal is served by the approve operation on a Draft version with MSG-P6-005 and status 422.

title: Allowed body file types and the size limit are marked assumed and fixed by no source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 13 configuration and reference data; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1
description: The legacy story sets the property rwb.comms.template.allowed-types to DOCX and the property rwb.comms.template.max-size-mb to 10, and marks the second as assumed. No source fixes the allowed list, the size limit or who owns the values, and TSD P6 T3.1 gives body_ref as an ATTACHMENT of varchar(400) with no type or size rule.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 13 'property `rwb.comms.template.max-size-mb` = 10, assumed'; no list or limit in TSD P6 v2 T3.1
proposed: Keep DOCX and 10 MB as the Epic 1 configuration defaults, read as configuration and never in Java, and record the values as the configuration owner's to confirm before the first SIT run.

title: Template body container: own Blob store or a P5 rwb-document object
source: Legacy RWB-E1-034 sections 3 and 13; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-REF-050); Ownership Map v1
description: The legacy story stores the body write-once through the ACE storage pattern and returns body_ref, and TSD P6 T3.1 gives body_ref as a claim-check ATTACHMENT. The Ownership Map gives the document entities to P5 rwb-document, so whether the object behind body_ref is a document-hub object of rwb-document or an object of this service's own container is not stated; nor is whether a document row must exist for a template body.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 13 'TemplateBodyStore ... through the ACE storage pattern and returns body_ref'; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 DF-REF-050 body_ref ATTACHMENT; ownership.json template/merge_field to P6 and document/document_custody to P5
proposed: Store the body write-once in this service's own Blob container and keep only body_ref, so no P5 contract is needed in wave 1; switch to a document-hub object through the rwb-document contract when that contract names one.

title: Retention is module P6 in the story and P5 rwb-document in the ownership map, and no C row declares the retention contract
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3 (heading RWB-E4-042, module line and Data table); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.21; Ownership Map v1 (retention_rule, retention_action, document, document_type and case_document_check owner P5); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44; split plan rows RWB-P6-E4042-APP and RWB-P6-E4042-CON
description: RWB-E4-042 is a module P6 Communications story of FEAT-COM-08, it depends FEAT-DCM-17 and its subject is the retention class, and its Data table lists recovery_case, notice, document, decision_log_entry, rule_row and template. In the target the notice and its class belong to two services. The Ownership Map gives retention_rule, retention_action, document, document_type and case_document_check to P5 rwb-document; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P5 metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures and retention; slide 44 gives JOB-17 to rwb-document; and P6 owns notice, template and merge_field only. Both slices of this key carry an empty contract dependency list, so neither story can name the rwb-document contract it must read the class from, and no P5 operation of the ownership map reads the retention class of a document. The stories therefore read the class as a consumed and faked answer and state that this service owns no class, no period and no disposal.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-042: "| Module | P6 Communications |" and "| Depends on | FEAT-DCM-17 |"; FSD P6 A2.21.2: "Integration points. the Workbench document hub, Blob storage"; Ownership Map v1: retention_rule owner P5, basis "Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 P5 (retention), slide 16 P5 DB line and slide 44 JOB-17 (rwb-document)"; Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-17 Retention owner rwb-document, mechanism Schedule.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-042 (module line, Data table, Endpoints, section 19)
proposed: Keep the closure gate in rwb-comms and the retention itself in rwb-document: add the rwb-document retention-class read as a C row of RWB-P6-E4042-APP when P5 publishes the operation, the nearest published baseline being RWB-P5-AD021-CON retention classes and legal hold; fix the path and the answer of that read in RWB-P6-E4042-CON; and record in the Service Contract Catalog that rwb-comms reads a class and never sets one.

title: No source names a retention-coverage operation, its answer shape or its access right
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.21; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3 (heading RWB-E4-042, Endpoints, Screen and states); Ownership Map v1 API rows of P5 rwb-document
description: The TSD P6 endpoint inventory lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 and none of them is a retention or a coverage operation; the legacy story names only the notice request and the notice read of API-P6-001 and API-P6-002, its screen is SCR-33 Template approval, and the FSD A2.21 describes an unattended run with no operation at all. The P5 API rows of the ownership map carry the document reads, the checklist read, the custody read and the review rows, and no read of a document retention class. The baseline therefore fixes one read of its own under the service base, GET /cases/{caseId}/retention-coverage with a 200 answer of one entry per notice document (noticeId, caseId, documentId, noticeType, classPresent), capability area Documents with right R and scope applied, errors 401, 403, 404 and 503, and no Idempotency-Key, and it marks the path as fixed by this baseline. The field types, the page shape and an optional class code element are not given by any source.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 last row: "| API-P6-011 | POST | /api/recovery/v1/signature-requests/{requestId}/result | Treatment and offer U | E2 |"; legacy RWB-E4-042 Endpoints: the notice POST and the notice GET only; FSD P6 A2.21.4 has one main success flow row and no operation row.
proposed: Adopt GET /cases/{caseId}/retention-coverage on /api/recovery/comms/v1 as fixed by D-RCV-60 in the rwb-comms OpenAPI file and in the Service Contract Catalog, with the five elements of an entry and the boolean presence fact, and settle the field types, the page shape and an optional class code in the RWB-P6-E4042-CON baseline review with the gateway-bff and rwb-document owners.

title: The hold of the closure and the Document Hub task of R-WO-48 have no operation, no body and no message
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-48; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.21.2 and A2.21.4.3; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3 (heading RWB-E4-042, Validation and messages, Permission checks); Ownership Map v1 (task, timer owner P3; document_hub_parameter owner P5)
description: R-WO-48 gives the from state RETENTION_RUNNING, the event RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING, the condition, the action "Hold closure and raise a Document Hub task", the to state RETENTION_RUNNING, the owner Operational Excellence, the system Document Hub and the timer of 5 working days. The FSD A2.21.2 step 3 says only "raises a task where a person is needed", and the legacy story has no message for a missing class in its Validation and messages table and lists only the Litigation rights of the notice endpoints in its Permission checks. The Ownership Map gives task and timer to P3 rwb-case, so the hold and the task are rwb-case state and rwb-case work, and no source names the operation, the body or the reason-code contract through which rwb-comms asks for them, and no source gives the message a missing class shows.
evidence: R-WO-48 row: "Hold closure and raise a Document Hub task | RETENTION_RUNNING | Operational Excellence | Document Hub | 5 working days"; FSD P6 A2.21.2 step 3: "Writes the decision log entry; raises a task where a person is needed"; Ownership Map: task owner P3, timer owner P3.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-042 (AC1, Validation and messages, Permission checks)
proposed: Fix one case-fact operation on the rwb-case contract that carries the case ID and the reason code RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING of R-WO-48, holds the closure and raises the Document Hub task with its 5 working days in rwb-case, declare it as consumed and faked in RWB-P6-E4042-CON with a placeholder on its body, and take the message of a missing class and of a refused fact from the rwb-case message standard when that owner publishes it.

title: The retention classes, the class per document type and the periods are unset and are not this service's data
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-DCM-010, REQ-DCM-019, NFR-028 and NFR-074; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2; Ownership Map v1 (retention_rule, retention_action owner P5)
description: NFR-028 says every document type carries a retention class and the class sets how long the document is kept, with the target "Retention classes defined per type; periods not set" and the status "Open, DL26"; REQ-DCM-010 requires a class on every document, and REQ-DCM-019 and NFR-074 require a recorded decision on a disposal or an extension. The P6 list of values holds LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-LANG, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-SENT-TYPE, LOV-SIGN-METHOD, LOV-SIGN-STATUS and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS, and no retention list appears in any source, nor the class codes or the mapping of a document type to a class. None of it is data of this service: the story needs only the presence or the absence of a class per notice document, so the codes and the periods stay P5 reference data and their absence blocks no rule of this key.
evidence: NFR-028: "Every document type carries a retention class, and the class sets how long the document is kept. | Retention classes defined per type; periods not set | Open, DL26"; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 lists nine value sets and none is a retention class; Ownership Map: retention_rule and retention_action owner P5.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-042 (AC1, Data table row template and document)
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer with the Data steward
proposed: Close DL26 with the retention class list and the class per document type in rwb-document as the owner of the reference data, carry the class code through the coverage read as the owner returns it, and keep every period and every disposal rule out of this service so that no story of this key validates, defaults or maps a class.

title: Screen SCR-33, the legacy permission checks and the FSD background-event row do not fit an unattended retention check
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3 (heading RWB-E4-042, Screen and states, Permission checks); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.21.3.3 and A2.21.4.4 (and A2.20.4.4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-47 and R-WO-49 to R-WO-51
description: The legacy Screen and states table names SCR-33 Template approval in the states Draft, approved and withdrawn, and its Permission checks list Litigation right C for RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE and Litigation right R for thirty roles. The FSD A2.21.3.3 gives the primary actor as "None; runs unattended" with the Compliance and PDPA officer as the second actor, and FSD A2.21.4.4 gives the background event AC-BG-P6-021-01 "WIN outbound notices | Schedule | Daily 16:00 | Writes approved notices to WIN | Notices dispatched the same day | Notice periods start on time", which repeats the row AC-BG-P6-020-01 of A2.20 word for word and belongs to the notice dispatch capability. The only closing state any source names is CASE_CLOSED of R-WO-47, which R-WO-49 to R-WO-51 also use, and the set of states that mean the case closes is enumerated nowhere.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-042 Screen and states: "| SCR-33 Template approval | Draft; approved; withdrawn |"; FSD P6 A2.21.4.4 row AC-BG-P6-021-01 identical to A2.20.4.4 row AC-BG-P6-020-01; R-WO-47 to state CASE_CLOSED.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-042 (Screen and states, Permission checks, AC1)
proposed: Keep SCR-33 with the template capability of the same module and show the coverage on the case record documents panel through the gateway-bff composite route; take the trigger from the consumed CaseStateChanged event with the closing state CASE_CLOSED of R-WO-47 and the rest of the state vocabulary as data of rwb-case; and record AC-BG-P6-021-01 as a copy of AC-BG-P6-020-01 that belongs to the notice dispatch capability and not to a retention run.

title: Template ownership is a conflict between DL28 and the catalogue, and the split of the surface between RWB-E1-034 and RWB-AD-017 is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-AD-017 (metadata row Decision, the Endpoints table and the Permission checks table); Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10 DL28; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (template, merge_field); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1; legacy RWB-E1-034 (metadata row, Flow steps 4 to 8)
description: Two different points of this key are settled by no single source. First, the legacy story cites DL28, which answers the ownership question with the document module, while Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map give template and merge_field to P6 rwb-comms; under the precedence rule the catalogue wins and DL28 loses, but the loser has to be recorded and the ownership of the wording has to be stated once. Second, the two legacy stories RWB-E1-034 and RWB-AD-017 both upload, approve and withdraw a template version, and no source states which of them owns which part of the surface: the Epic 1 story builds the five operations and the screen, the Epic 8 story describes the same approve and withdraw on SCR-33 with a paged administration list that no Epic 1 text has. Third, the legacy Endpoints table of the thin story names the notice request and the notice read of the communications module and not one template operation, and its Permission checks table names the Litigation right while the TSD appendix T-A.1 puts the five template operations on the Documents right, so the legacy permission rows cannot be used as they stand.
evidence: Decision Log v10 DL28: "Who owns the letter templates and the fields filled into them? | A: the document module owns templates and fields; Legal approves wording."; ownership.json: "template" owner "P6" basis "Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery)"; legacy RWB-AD-017 Endpoints: "POST | /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices | Litigation C" and "GET | /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId} | Litigation R"; TSD P6 T-A.1: "API-P6-003 | GET | /api/recovery/v1/admin/templates | Documents R | E1"; Legacy RWB-E1-034 Flow step 6: "System: checks the role (Documents A), that the approver is not the uploader (CTL-05) ... sets state Approved".
legacy_ref: RWB-AD-017 (metadata row, Endpoints, Permission checks); RWB-E1-034 (Flow, section 12)
proposed: Record in the Change Register that template and merge_field are P6 rwb-comms and that DL28 is superseded by Architecture v5 slide 41 under the precedence rule, and fix the split in the plan: RWB-P6-E1034-APP keeps the Epic 1 upload-and-approve core word for word and RWB-P6-AD017-APP delivers the Epic 8 administration surface (the paged list, the body download, the approve with a valid from date, the withdraw with a reason and the litigation officer task). Confirm the Documents right of T-A.1 as the right of the five operations and retire the Litigation rows of the legacy permission table.

title: The reference lists the template screen needs have no contract row and no DP-07 in this key
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (product_group, channel, notice_type, signature_basis) and T3.2; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (lov_value, reference_row, reference_version to P3); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-07 and §R3 default ruling; B-P6-03 JSON line RWB-P6-AD017-APP (patterns, C rows)
description: The upload validates product group, channel, notice type and signature basis against the lists of TSD P6 T3.2, and the administration list filters on the same values. Under the default ruling those lists are reference data of P3 rwb-case, and DP-07 adds the dependency pair H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON. This key carries none of that: its patterns applied are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only and its contract dependencies are empty, so the read of the four lists cannot be declared as a consumed contract of this story and the plan has no row for it. The values are LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-NOTICE and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS as TSD P6 T3.2 gives them.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1: "DF-REF-049 | product_group | LOV | varchar(15) | No | LOV-PRODUCT | Workbench" and "DF-REF-068 | signature_basis | LOV | varchar(20) | No | LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS | Workbench"; TSD P6 v2 T3.2: "LOV-CHANNEL | MOBILE, HOME_PHONE, WORK_PHONE, LINE, EMAIL, POSTAL_ADDRESS, CALL, VISIT, SMS, LETTER, PORTAL, BRANCH"; Template and Rules v1 DP-07: "Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON"; ownership.json: "lov_value" owner "P3" ruling "lov_value is reference data and stays with P3 (R-PREC default ruling, DP-07)".
legacy_ref: RWB-AD-017 (Data table: template product_group; validation table); RWB-E1-034 (DB6, AC4)
proposed: Add DP07 to the pattern set of this key and the rows H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON at the next plan revision, so that the four lists are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case with the version in force. Until that row exists the lists are validated against the value sets loaded by the template catalogue story of the same service and the placeholder stands in the story and in the contract.

title: The withdrawal reason, the field that holds it and the decision code of an approval or a withdrawal are not stated
source: Legacy RWB-AD-017 (AC1, AC2, Validation and messages); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (template fields DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-069) and appendix T-A.2 (API-P6-006, API-P6-007); legacy RWB-E1-034 (BR5, section 14, AC8); Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 P6 A2.1 BR-P6-001
section: 3; 8; 11; 14 of RWB-P6-AD017-APP; 3; 11; 14; AC2; AC3 of RWB-P6-AD017-CON
description: The two legacy criteria carry no value: AC1 says a Legal approval happens and AC2 says a template is withdrawn, and neither gives a rule for the withdrawal reason, a decision code for the approval or the withdrawal, or a rule id to record. The Epic 1 story gives the valid from rule (today or later, MSG-GEN-003) and the self-approval refusal, and those are kept as they are, but it gives no rule for the reason beyond a non-empty field, and no column of template holds it: TSD P6 T3.1 defines DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-069 and none is a withdrawal reason, while the screen shows one and the request carries one. In the same way the local decision record needs a decision code and a rule id and no source names either for a template approval or a withdrawal, so no code can be written without inventing it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-017 AC2: "Given a template withdrawn"; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 template: "DF-REF-050 | body_ref ... DF-REF-051 | approved_by_legal ... DF-REF-065 | valid_from" and no withdrawal field; TSD P6 v2 T-A.2 API-P6-007: "Purpose | Withdraw an approved template version with a reason | Request | TemplateWithdrawal"; Legacy RWB-E1-034 section 14: "MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty | Enter {field}."; FSD P6 A2.1 BR-P6-001: "No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version".
legacy_ref: RWB-AD-017 (AC1, AC2, Validation and messages); RWB-E1-034 (BR5, section 14)
proposed: Record the reason in the local decision record of the withdrawal through the library and keep the non-empty check as the only rule until the business owner publishes a length and content rule; keep the template row the shape TSD P6 T3.1 gives it. Publish the decision code and the rule id of a template approval and of a template withdrawal with that rule, and hold both unset in the story until they are named. The valid from rule of RWB-E1-034 and the Documents right of T-A.1 stand as they are.

title: The task target of a withdrawn template and the resumption of held generation are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-06; Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 P6 A2.1 AC-EXC-P6-001-02 and VR-P6-001-1; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (notice) and T3.3; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (task to P3)
description: R-LIT-04 holds generation when the template of a notice is withdrawn and raises a task to the litigation officer, and the FSD shows that task raised by the 16:00 notice run with MSG-P6-003. No source names the operation that creates a task, the task code, the target queue or the fields the task carries, and the task table is rwb-case's, so this story can only call a contract whose operation is unnamed. R-LIT-06 says generation resumes on the current version once a new version is approved by Legal, inside one working day, but no source says whether the resumption is driven by the approval, by the next run or by a task closure, and no source says how a held notice of the withdrawn version is re-pointed at the new version. The 1 working day target of R-LIT-04 is also not an operational value of this service.
evidence: R-LIT-04: "NOTICE_GENERATED | TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN | template_status = withdrawn | Hold generation and raise a task to the litigation officer | NOTICE_BLOCKED | Litigation officer | Workbench, the Workbench document hub | 1 working day"; R-LIT-06: "NOTICE_BLOCKED | TEMPLATE_REPLACED | a new template version is approved by Legal | Resume generation on the current version | NOTICE_GENERATED | Workbench | Rules component, the Workbench document hub | 1 working day"; FSD P6 A2.1 AC-EXC-P6-001-02: "notice \"N-0101\" is \"Held\" with hold reason \"TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN\" and is not in the WIN file And a task is raised to the litigation officer team with MSG-P6-003"; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice has no task field and T3.3 has no task relationship.
proposed: Agree with the rwb-case owner the operation, task code, target queue and fields of the litigation officer task, with the template code, the version, the language, the case, the notice type and MSG-P6-003 as its content, and record the code and the queue as configuration in the service values file. Record that the resumption is applied by RWB-P6-E1052-APP when it reads the current version at its next run, and that this story neither repoints a notice nor closes a task.

title: No template event exists in the service event catalogue
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (event catalogue); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.3; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (template, merge_field to P6)
description: An approval and a withdrawal change the wording every later notice uses, and no event reports either. The catalogue holds three events of this service on rwb.comms.events.v1, NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered, and nothing for a template version, and the TSD event table names the same three. A consumer that needs the fact therefore has to read the template state through this service's read operation, and no consumer outside the service is named today because the generation that reads the state lives in the same service. The contract must not invent an event, so the absence is recorded as a gap rather than filled.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42: "13 | NoticeGenerated | rwb-comms | rwb.comms.events.v1 | rwb-decision", "14 | NoticeDispatched | rwb-comms | rwb.comms.events.v1 | rwb-reporting", "15 | NoticeDelivered | rwb-comms | rwb.comms.events.v1 | rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee, rwb-case" and no template row; TSD P6 v2 T5.3: "NoticeGenerated | Published | NoticeDispatched | Published | NoticeDelivered | Published".
proposed: Record in the Event and Messaging document that a template approval and a withdrawal publish no event and that a consumer reads the template state through the read operation of rwb-comms, and allocate a template event in the catalogue only when a consumer outside rwb-comms needs the fact; the contract of this key declares the absence and an absence test keeps it.

title: No published rwb-document operation for the discovery production, and no C row for the document contract this key reads
source: Program BRD v4 section 5.5 (REQ-DCM-017, REQ-DCM-018); FSD P5 A2.6 and A2.4; TSD P6 v2 T5.2 and appendix T-A.1; Ownership Map v1
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The document side of the answer is rwb-document's: the document, its version history and the court attributes of a produced document (REQ-DCM-017, REQ-DCM-018). No source publishes an operation that produces a discovery set, and the Ownership Map holds no contract row for one, so the key has no C dependency and the story reads the published document and content reads of P5 with the discovery production left as a P5 obligation marked with the placeholder.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T5.2 names P5 for documents, and its appendix T-A.1 lists eleven P6 endpoints, none a discovery or document-request operation; the Ownership Map P5 API rows hold document, content, version, custody, checklist, intake, review and field-capture paths and no discovery path; FSD P5 A2.6 (FEAT-DCM-06) describes a search across cases and no production; REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018 state the outcome of an electronic discovery request and name no operation.
proposed: P5 rwb-document publishes one discovery operation under /api/recovery/document/v1 with its request and answer, and the C row of that contract is added to this story. Until then the story reads the document metadata, the version list and the content operation of P5 and marks the production, the court attributes and the selector with this placeholder.

title: No document-request operation, answer shape, decision code or rule id in any source
source: Legacy RWB-E4-041 Endpoints and Data; FSD P6 A2.20; TSD P6 v2 appendix T-A.1 and T3.1; Ownership Map v1
section: 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.7 Tables owned; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story answers a document request with the two notice operations of another feature, and no source names a document-request operation of rwb-comms, a request or answer shape, a request table, a decision code or a rule id for the answer. The contract story fixes the two operations under /api/recovery/comms/v1, the answer shape, the two tables and the record element, and marks the field-level detail, the decision code and the rule id with the placeholder.
evidence: The Endpoints table of RWB-E4-041 names POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 has no document-request endpoint and T3.1 no request table; FSD P6 A2.20 gives a main-success criterion and two exception criteria and no field shape, decision code or rule id of an answer; the Ownership Map has no document-request row for P6.
proposed: RWB-P6-E4041-CON publishes POST /cases/{caseId}/document-requests and GET /document-requests/{requestId} under /api/recovery/comms/v1, the DocumentRequest and DocumentRequestAnswer shapes, the document_request and document_request_entry tables and the record element; the field types, the decision code and the rule id are confirmed by the rwb-decision owner and the business before the app story is done.

title: Selector conflict: REQ-DCM-017 asks for a named population and the legacy story answers per case
source: Program BRD v4 section 5.5 (REQ-DCM-017); legacy RWB-E4-041 Story, Endpoints and Data; FSD P6 A2.20
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules (BR8, BR9); 12.2 REST operations consumed; 19 Out of scope
description: REQ-DCM-017 produces every document for a named population, which is a selector across cases and documents, while the legacy story and the FSD describe the answer for one case and the legacy Data table is keyed on notice.case_id. The two scopes are not the same request and no source decides which one the service serves.
evidence: REQ-DCM-017 reads producing every document for a named population; the RWB-E4-041 Story and its Data table are per case and its permission checks are applied on a case; FSD P6 A2.20.2 has a single case-bound screen flow and no population selector.
proposed: The rwb-comms operation stays per case, as the path and the legacy story describe it, and the population selector of REQ-DCM-017 is served by the rwb-document discovery production; a cross-case answer is out of scope of this key until the two owners agree one shape.

title: The legacy rows of RWB-E4-041 are carried over from notice generation
source: Legacy RWB-E4-041 Screen and states, Validation and messages, Endpoints and Permission checks; FSD P6 A2.20.1 and A2.20.3.1
section: 2 Business rationale; 10 Authority; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story names SCR-33 Template approval as the screen of a document request, carries VR-P6-020-1 (the withdrawn-template rule of R-LIT-04 with MSG-P6-003) as its validation rule, names the two notice operations with Litigation rights, and the FSD metric and problem statement of A2.20 are the notice-and-proof metric of the letter features. None of these rows belongs to a document request.
evidence: RWB-E4-041 Screen and states is SCR-33 Template approval; its Validation and messages table is the notice message set (MSG-P6-003, MSG-P6-004, MSG-P6-001); its Endpoints are POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} with Litigation C and R; FSD P6 A2.20.1 repeats the measure notices with proof of delivery and the problem of letters prepared by hand.
proposed: The rows are named as the notice feature's and not copied into this key: the screen of the answer belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen stories, the withdrawn-template rule belongs to the template stories of rwb-comms, and the capability area of both operations is Documents with right R as TSD P6 T6.1 holds it.

title: The answer format and the protection of a produced document are not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E4-041 Story and Acceptance criteria; Program BRD v4 REQ-DCM-018; FSD P5 A2.4; TSD P6 v2 T3.1
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.3 Events published; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy criterion asks for the documents and the index entries and does not say whether the answer is a file, an archive or a list, how a produced document is protected and certified (REQ-DCM-018), or what the service stores of it. No source names the answer medium, the archive or export file, the pending state of a copy that is not yet stored, or the readers record.
evidence: RWB-E4-041 AC1 reads returns the documents and the index entries a legal or audit request asks for and names no medium; REQ-DCM-018 lists the origin, the entry date, the alteration flag and the readers of a produced document and no medium; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 declares no file or archive column for P6 and holds body_ref as a varchar(400) attachment reference only.
proposed: The answer is a JSON list of index entries and document lines with a reference per produced document, the bytes are fetched on the rwb-document content operation as a claim-check, and an archive or export file is not an operation of this baseline; the archived file and its protection are a P5 decision under REQ-DCM-018 and REQ-DCM-020.

title: document_custody is a P6 module table in the legacy story and a P5 rwb-document table in the target, and the P5 custody contract has no C row and no contract story
source: Legacy RWB-E4-040 Data table (document, document_custody, DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011, DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.19; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T5.2; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A.1 (API-P5-007); Ownership Map tables (document, document_custody owned by P5) and api (POST /documents/{documentId}/custody owned by P5); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44; WP B-P6-03 story lines RWB-P6-E4040-APP and RWB-P6-E4040-CON (C [])
section: Metadata table (Contract dependencies), section 2 Business rationale, section 3 Preconditions, section 10 Authority, section 11 Data, 12.2 REST operations consumed, 12.7 Tables owned, 13 Solution plan, 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy key states its data in the recovery schema of one module and lists document and document_custody as P6 Communications rows, so a custody movement was a row next to the notice. Architecture v5 gives the document hub to P5 rwb-document (metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures and retention on slide 41, the rwb_document schema on slide 16 and JOB-17 on slide 44) and the Ownership Map gives document and document_custody to P5, so the physical document and every movement of it are another service rows. TSD P6 T3.1 defines notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and no custody table. The P5 custody operation is in the Ownership Map as the api row POST /documents/{documentId}/custody owned by P5 (API-P5-007 in TSD P5 appendix T-A.1), but the plan gives both stories of this key C [] and names no P5 contract story that would carry the operation, so the C row and the story it points to are absent from the plan while the call is unavoidable.
evidence: RWB-E4-040 lists document id, case_id, person_key, document_type, source, storage_ref and 5 more (DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011) and document_custody id, document_id, moved_at, from_location, to_location, held_by and 1 more (DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024) under Module P6 Communications. TSD P6 v2 T3.1 defines notice, template, merge_field and signature_request only, and T5.2 sends document questions to P5. Ownership Map tables: document and document_custody owner P5, basis Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD P5 T3.1. Ownership Map api: POST /documents/{documentId}/custody owner P5. WP B-P6-03: RWB-P6-E4040-APP H [RWB-P6-E4040-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON], C [].
owner_role: solution architect with the P5 rwb-document owner
proposed: Keep the target owner and write it into both stories: document and document_custody are P5 rows in rwb_document, rwb-comms declares no custody table, no custody column and no cross-schema key, records the movement through the P5 custody operation one hop away with a 2 s budget, and keeps only the identifier of the movement on its notice. Step D1 adds the C row of the P5 custody contract and of its fake to both stories when the P5 contract story is planned.

title: No custody operation and no requirement exist for the custody movement in the P6 specification, so both operations, their rights and their message IDs are new
source: Legacy RWB-E4-040 Endpoints table and validation messages; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.19 and the Requirements served table; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 and T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17
section: Metadata table, section 1 Story, section 4 Flow, section 5 Exception paths, section 10 Authority, 12.1 REST operations provided, 14 Validation and messages, 18 Traceability
description: The legacy key has no operation of its own: its Endpoints table copies the notice POST and the notice GET of the monolith base, and the movement itself is described only as a data table and as one acceptance criterion. The endpoint inventory of the TSD P6 holds eleven operations and none of them is a custody, movement or document-request operation, and the FSD A2.19 gives only the intent, the integration point, the prerequisite and the roles. The requirement list of the module has no row for FEAT-COM-06 either, so the new surface has no requirement ID behind it. The consequence is fixed rather than invented: the contract story declares two new operations under the service base, the Documents right C and R read from the matrix of TSD P6 T6.1, the error set of the platform, and the placeholder on every message ID the sources do not give.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011: notices, admin templates, messages, signature requests. FSD P6 A2.19.2 gives integration point the Workbench document hub and prerequisite FEAT-DCM-19 and no step that names an operation; A2.19.4 gives one success criterion and two exception criteria and no endpoint. The Requirements served table of the FSD P6 runs REQ-OCC-001 to REQ-OCC-020 and none is FEAT-COM-06 or custody. Legacy RWB-E4-040 Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/notices Litigation C and GET /notices/{noticeId} Litigation R, both of the notice and neither of a movement.
owner_role: rwb-comms tech lead with the P6 module owner
proposed: RWB-P6-E4040-CON fixes two new operations under /api/recovery/comms/v1, POST and GET /notices/{noticeId}/custody-movements, with the Documents right C and R and scope applied, the platform error set and the placeholder on the message IDs; the app story implements them and raises no message text the sources do not give.

title: The movement field set of the rwb-comms answer is not specified: the seventh document_custody field, the field types and required flags, and the notice-side reference column
source: Legacy RWB-E4-040 Data table (document_custody, DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (document_custody) and T3.2 (LOV-CUSTODY); FSD P6 A2.19
section: section 11 Data, 12.1 REST operations provided, 12.7 Tables owned, 12.8 Contract fakes, 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy data table names six fields of document_custody and says and 1 more for the seventh, and it names no type, no length and no required flag. The P6 data model has no custody object, so no P6 source fixes the types of the fields on this service answer or the name of the column that keeps the movement reference on notice. The whole table definition, types and list values included, belongs to the P5 document hub and is the owner to publish. The consequence: the contract story fixes seven field names, five of them named by the legacy data, marks the seventh and the types with the placeholder, and fixes the notice-side reference as a nullable column of notice in rwb_comms; the app story writes and reads only what the baseline fixes.
evidence: RWB-E4-040 Data table row document_custody: id, document_id, moved_at, from_location, to_location, held_by and 1 more, with DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024, and no module of the P6 TSD defines the table. TSD P6 v2 T3.1 ends at signature_request. TSD P5 v2 T3.1 defines document_custody with seven fields and T3.2 gives LOV-CUSTODY for the two location fields, which is the owner definition and not a P6 one. No source names a column on notice that holds a movement reference.
owner_role: rwb-comms tech lead with the P5 rwb-document owner
proposed: The baseline fixes the seven names and the request fields, takes the types of the six named fields from the owner definition, and carries the seventh field and every type as the placeholder until the P5 custody contract is published; the notice-side reference is a nullable column of notice, added by one per-service Flyway step, holding the owner identifier of the latest movement.

title: The decision code and the rule id of a custody movement are not stated in any source
source: Legacy RWB-E4-040 header (Decision None), AC1 and AC2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.19.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-20, R-UNI-39); TSD P6 Communications v2 T2
section: section 2 Business rationale, section 8 Business rules (BR3, BR11), 12.3 Events published, 13 Solution plan, 18 Traceability
description: The legacy criterion says the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version, and it names neither a decision code nor a rule id for the movement. The header of the legacy story says Decision None, the FSD A2.19 gives only BR-P6-019 (no value in code) and the validation rule of a stale data product, and the business rules of the target name R-UNI-20 (a legal hold stops every outbound action and automated decision) and R-UNI-39 (an incident on an unrecorded decision) but no rule of a custody movement. The decision record is nevertheless mandatory before the change, so its element is fixed and its two values are carried as the placeholder to be settled by the owner of the decision types, never invented by this key.
evidence: RWB-E4-040 AC1: the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version. RWB-E4-040 header: Decision None. FSD P6 A2.19.3.1: VR-P6-019-1 and BR-P6-019 only. TSD P6 T2: CommunicationsService writes the decision log entry before any change, with no code. No row of the data table of the legacy story names a custody decision.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P6 module owner
proposed: The baseline declares the decision-record element of a movement in full and carries the decision code and the rule id as the placeholder; the app story writes the record through the local library before the change, takes the rule version from the library, and fails closed with MSG-P7-003 and an incident under R-UNI-39 when the record cannot be written.

title: Whether a movement is allowed on a closed case, on a case under legal hold and in which notice states is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E4-040 AC1 (Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.19.4 (no alternate flow); TSD P6 Communications v2 T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-20); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (EV-05)
section: section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow, section 5 Exception paths (X1, X6), section 8 Business rules (BR4, BR5), section 9 State transitions, 12.4 Events consumed
description: The legacy criterion starts from the data and the rule version being in place and names no notice state, no case state and no hold. The FSD A2.19 has no alternate flow, the TSD P6 states that the module has no state machine of its own and R-UNI-20 names the legal hold without naming which action it blocks for an original. The target therefore fixes the shape and leaves the values to their owners: the eligible notice states are a parameter of the service, a legal hold on the case refuses the movement under R-UNI-20, and the closure of a case reaches the service as the consumed CaseStateChanged event of the catalogue, whose local projection is not specified. The value of the parameter and the closure rule are settled at the baseline review and never written in code.
evidence: RWB-E4-040 AC1: Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place, with no state named. FSD P6 A2.19.4.2 alternate flows: None, No alternate path. TSD P6 T4: No case state machine of its own; the module acts on events from P3. Architecture v5 slide 42 row 05 CaseStateChanged: consumer rwb-comms, which is the only closure fact the catalogue gives this service.
owner_role: P6 module owner with the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: The eligible notice states are read as the parameter rwb.comms.custody.eligible-states, set at the baseline review; a legal hold refuses the movement under R-UNI-20; a closed case refuses it on the consumed CaseStateChanged fact; and the story tests the refusal paths behind the fakes without fixing a value in code.
